title.zh: 卷一百四十 志2: 曆志
title.raw: 卷一百四十 志2: 曆志 Volume 140: Treatises 2 Calendars

sentences.zh: 古先哲王，受命而帝天下者，必先觀象以垂法，治曆以明時，使萬物服其化風，四海同其正朔，然後能允釐下土，欽若上天。

translations.literal: Ancient sage-kings who received the Mandate and took Heaven as emperor over all under Heaven must first observe the signs to hand down models, regulate the calendar to clarify the seasons, make the myriad things submit to their transforming wind, and make the four seas share one new-year reckoning—only then could they truly bring order to the lands below and reverently accord with Heaven above.
translations.idiomatic: The sage-kings of antiquity who received the Mandate and ruled the world always began by reading the heavens to establish law, and by fixing the calendar to mark the seasons, so that all creation bowed to their civilizing influence and the four seas kept a single calendar—only then could they truly govern the earth below and stand in reverent harmony with Heaven.

sentences.zh: 故虞舜之紹唐堯，先齊七政；

translations.literal: Therefore when Yu Shun succeeded Tang Yao, he first aligned the Seven Regulators;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Shun succeeded Yao, his first act was to align the seven luminaries;

sentences.zh: 武王之得箕子，首敘九疇。

translations.literal: when King Wu obtained Jizi, he first set forth the Nine Categories.
translations.idiomatic: and when King Wu received Jizi, he began by expounding the Nine Categories.

sentences.zh: 皇極由是而允興，人時以之而不忒。

translations.literal: The Supreme Norm was thereby truly established, and human seasons through it were without error.
translations.idiomatic: The royal norm was thereby truly established, and the seasons of human affairs kept true to it without deviation.

translations.literal: From successive generations downward, which did not proceed from this.
translations.idiomatic: Every dynasty since has followed this same path.

sentences.zh: 粵自軒黃，肇正天統，歲躔辛卯，曆法時成。

translations.literal: From Xuanyuan and Huangdi onward, the celestial cycle was first rectified; the year marched to xinmao, and the calendrical method was then completed.
translations.idiomatic: From the age of the Yellow Emperor, the celestial order was first set right; when the year reached xinmao, the calendar was brought to completion.

sentences.zh: 故黃帝始用《辛卯曆》，顓頊次用《乙卯曆》，虞用《戊午曆》，夏用《丙寅曆》，商用《甲寅曆》，周用《丁巳曆》，魯用《庚子曆》，秦用《乙卯曆》。

translations.literal: Thus Huangdi first used the Xinmao Calendar; Zhuanxu next used the Yimao Calendar; Yu used the Wuwu Calendar; Xia used the Bingyin Calendar; Shang used the Jiayin Calendar; Zhou used the Dingsi Calendar; Lu used the Gengzi Calendar; Qin used the Yimao Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor first adopted the Xinmao Calendar; Zhuanxu next the Yimao; the Yu dynasty the Wuwu; Xia the Bingyin; Shang the Jiayin; Zhou the Dingsi; Lu the Gengzi; and Qin the Yimao.

sentences.zh: 漢用《太初曆》、《四分曆》、《三統曆》，凡三本。

translations.literal: Han used the Taichu Calendar, the Sifen Calendar, and the Santong Calendar—three works in all.
translations.idiomatic: Han employed the Taichu, Sifen, and Santong calendars—three in all.

sentences.zh: 魏用《黃初曆》、《景初曆》，凡二本。

translations.literal: Wei used the Huangchu Calendar and the Jingchu Calendar—two works in all.
translations.idiomatic: Wei used the Huangchu and Jingchu calendars—two in all.

sentences.zh: 晉用《元始曆》、《合元萬分曆》，凡二本。

translations.literal: Jin used the Yuanshi Calendar and the Heyuan Wanfen Calendar—two works in all.
translations.idiomatic: Jin used the Yuanshi and Heyuan Wanfen calendars—two in all.

sentences.zh: 宋用《大明曆》、《元嘉曆》，凡二本。

translations.literal: Song used the Daming Calendar and the Yuanjia Calendar—two works in all.
translations.idiomatic: Song used the Daming and Yuanjia calendars—two in all.

sentences.zh: 齊用《天保曆》、《同章曆》、《正象曆》，凡三本。

translations.literal: Qi used the Tianbao Calendar, the Tongzhang Calendar, and the Zhengxiang Calendar—three works in all.
translations.idiomatic: Qi used the Tianbao, Tongzhang, and Zhengxiang calendars—three in all.

sentences.zh: 後魏用《興和曆》、《正光曆》、《正元曆》，凡三本。

translations.literal: Northern Wei used the Xinghe Calendar, the Zhengguang Calendar, and the Zhengyuan Calendar—three works in all.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Wei used the Xinghe, Zhengguang, and Zhengyuan calendars—three in all.

sentences.zh: 梁用《大同曆》、《乾象曆》、《永昌曆》，凡三本。

translations.literal: Liang used the Datong Calendar, the Qianxiang Calendar, and the Yongchang Calendar—three works in all.
translations.idiomatic: Liang used the Datong, Qianxiang, and Yongchang calendars—three in all.

sentences.zh: 後周用《天和曆》、《丙寅曆》、《明元曆》，凡三本。

translations.literal: Northern Zhou used the Tianhe Calendar, the Bingyin Calendar, and the Mingyuan Calendar—three works in all.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Zhou used the Tianhe, Bingyin, and Mingyuan calendars—three in all.

sentences.zh: 隋用《甲子曆》、《開皇曆》、《皇極曆》、《大業曆》，凡四本。

translations.literal: Sui used the Jiazi Calendar, the Kaihuang Calendar, the Huangji Calendar, and the Daye Calendar—four works in all.
translations.idiomatic: Sui used the Jiazi, Kaihuang, Huangji, and Daye calendars—four in all.

sentences.zh: 唐用《戊寅曆》、《麟德曆》、《神龍曆》、《大衍曆》、《元和觀象曆》、《長慶宣明曆》、《寶應曆》、《正元曆》、《景福崇元曆》，凡九本。

translations.literal: Tang used the Wuyin Calendar, the Linde Calendar, the Shenlong Calendar, the Dayan Calendar, the Yuanhe Guanxiang Calendar, the Changqing Xuanming Calendar, the Baoying Calendar, the Zhengyuan Calendar, and the Jingfu Chongyuan Calendar—nine works in all.
translations.idiomatic: Tang employed the Wuyin, Linde, Shenlong, Dayan, Yuanhe Guanxiang, Changqing Xuanming, Baoying, Zhengyuan, and Jingfu Chongyuan calendars—nine in all.

sentences.zh: 洎梁氏之應運也，乘唐室陵遲之後，黃巢離亂之餘，眾職未修，三辰孰驗。

translations.literal: When the Liang dynasty received the Mandate, riding on the decline of the Tang house and in the aftermath of Huang Chao's turmoil, the various offices were not restored, and who could verify the three luminaries?
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang came to power, in the wake of Tang's decline and Huang Chao's rebellion, government functions lay in disarray and no one could reliably track the heavens.

sentences.zh: 故當時歲曆，猶用《宣明》、《崇元》二法，參而成之。

translations.literal: Therefore the annual calendar of that time still used the two methods of the Xuanming and Chongyuan calendars, combining them to complete it.
translations.idiomatic: The court calendar of the day still drew on the Xuanming and Chongyuan systems, blending the two into one.

sentences.zh: 及晉祖肇位，司天監馬重績始造新曆，奉表上之，云：「臣聞為國者，正一氣之元，宣萬邦之命，爰資曆以立章程。

translations.literal: When the Jin founder first took the throne, the Director of the Astronomy Bureau Ma Chongji first devised a new calendar and submitted a memorial, saying: "Your subject has heard that to govern a state is to rectify the origin of the single qi and proclaim the mandate of the myriad states—one relies on the calendar to establish regulations."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin founder ascended the throne, Ma Chongji of the Directorate of Astronomy devised a new calendar and presented a memorial, writing: "I have heard that to rule a state is to fix the origin of cosmic breath and proclaim the mandate of all peoples—and for this one must rely on the calendar to set the standards of government."

sentences.zh: 《長慶宣明》，雖氣朔不渝，即星躔罕驗；

translations.literal: The Changqing Xuanming Calendar, though its qi and new moon did not change, yet its stellar positions were rarely verified;
translations.idiomatic: The Changqing Xuanming calendar kept its solar terms and new moons steady, yet its star positions seldom matched observation;

sentences.zh: 《景福崇元》，縱五曆甚正，而年差一日。

translations.literal: the Jingfu Chongyuan Calendar, though its five reckonings were very correct, yet differed by one day in the year.
translations.idiomatic: while the Jingfu Chongyuan, though its five reckonings were largely sound, drifted a full day in the annual count.

sentences.zh: 今以《宣明》氣朔，《崇元》星緯，二曆相參，方得符合。

translations.literal: Now, taking the qi and new moon of the Xuanming and the stellar tracks of the Chongyuan, the two calendars cross-referenced, only then could they accord.
translations.idiomatic: Only by taking the solar terms and new moons from Xuanming and the star tracks from Chongyuan, and cross-checking the two, could a satisfactory fit be achieved.

sentences.zh: 自古諸曆，皆以天正十一月為歲首，循太古甲子為上元，積歲彌多，差闊至甚。

translations.literal: From antiquity all calendars took the eleventh month of the celestial standard as the year's head, following the ancient jiazi as the superior origin; as accumulated years grew ever more, the discrepancy became very great.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity every calendar had taken the eleventh month as the year's beginning and traced its origin back to the primordial jiazi year—yet as centuries piled up, the error grew enormous.

sentences.zh: 臣改法定元，創為新曆一部二十一卷，七章上下經二卷，算草八卷，立成十二卷，取唐天寶十四載乙未，立為近元，以雨水正月朔為歲首。

translations.literal: Your subject has revised the law and fixed the origin, creating a new calendar in one set of twenty-one scrolls: two scrolls of the upper and lower classics of the seven chapters, eight scrolls of calculation drafts, and twelve scrolls of ready reckonings, taking the yiwei year of the fourteenth year of Tang Tianbao as the near origin and making the new moon of the first month at Rain Water the year's head.
translations.idiomatic: I have revised the constants and fixed a new origin, composing a calendar in twenty-one scrolls—two of canonical text in upper and lower parts, eight of computational drafts, and twelve of ready tables—taking the yiwei year of Tianbao 14 as the near origin and making the new moon of the first month at Rain Water the start of the year.

translations.literal: I respectfully proceed to the Gate of the Imperial Secretariat to present it."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully present it at the Gate of the Imperial Secretariat."

sentences.zh: （《玉海》：《調元曆》，蓋仿曹士蒍小曆之舊。

translations.literal: (Jade Sea: The Tiaoyuan Calendar largely followed the old small calendar of Cao Shuxun.
translations.idiomatic: (Jade Sea: The Tiaoyuan Calendar largely followed the tradition of Cao Shuxun's small calendar.

sentences.zh: 唐建中時，曹士蒍始變古法，以顯慶五年為上元，雨水為歲首。

translations.literal: In the Jianzhong era of Tang, Cao Shuxun first altered the ancient method, taking the fifth year of Xianqing as the superior origin and Rain Water as the year's head.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang's Jianzhong era, Cao Shuxun first broke with ancient practice, taking Xianqing 5 as the superior origin and Rain Water as the year's beginning.

translations.literal: The age called it the small calendar.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries called this the small calendar.)〉

sentences.zh: 晉高祖命司天少監趙仁锜、張文皓，秋官正徐皓，天文參謀趙延乂、杜升、杜崇龜等，以新曆與《宣明》、《崇元》考核得失。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Jin ordered the Vice Directors of the Astronomy Bureau Zhao Renqi and Zhang Wenhao, the Director of the Ministry of Rites Xu Hao, and the astronomical advisers Zhao Yanyi, Du Sheng, and Du Chonggui and others to test the new calendar against the Xuanming and Chongyuan calendars for gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Gaozu ordered Vice Directors Zhao Renqi and Zhang Wenhao of the Astronomy Bureau, Xu Hao of the Ministry of Rites, and astronomical advisers Zhao Yanyi, Du Sheng, and Du Chonggui to compare the new calendar against Xuanming and Chongyuan and judge its merits.

sentences.zh: 俾有司奉而行之，因賜號《調元曆》，仍命翰林學士承旨和凝撰序。

translations.literal: He had the responsible offices receive and implement it, and accordingly bestowed the name Tiaoyuan Calendar, further ordering Academician Expositor He Ning to compose the preface.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices were ordered to adopt and implement it; it was given the name Tiaoyuan Calendar, and Academician Expositor He Ning was commissioned to write its preface.

translations.literal: Several years afterward, the standards gradually drifted.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years its constants began to slip.

sentences.zh: 至周顯德二年，世宗以端明殿學士、左散騎常侍王樸明於曆算，乃命樸考而正之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiande of Zhou, Shizong, because Wang Pu, Academician of the Duanming Hall and Left Regular Attendant, was skilled in calendrical calculation, ordered Pu to examine and correct it.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou Xiande 2, Shizong, finding Wang Pu—Academician of the Duanming Hall and Left Regular Attendant—expert in calendrical science, commissioned him to review and revise the calendar.

sentences.zh: 樸奉詔歲餘，撰成《欽天曆》十五卷，上之。

translations.literal: Pu received the edict for more than a year and completed the Qintian Calendar in fifteen scrolls, presenting it.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year at the task, Pu completed the Qintian Calendar in fifteen scrolls and presented it to the throne.

translations.literal: The memorial said:
translations.idiomatic: His memorial read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞聖人之作也，在乎知天人之變者也。

translations.literal: Your subject has heard that what the sage creates lies in knowing the transformations of Heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that what the sage creates rests on knowing how Heaven and humanity change.

sentences.zh: 人情之動，則可以言知之；

translations.literal: When human sentiment moves, it may be known through words;
translations.idiomatic: The movements of human affairs may be known through language;

sentences.zh: 天道之動，則當以數知之。

translations.literal: when the Way of Heaven moves, it must be known through numbers.
translations.idiomatic: but the movements of Heaven must be known through number.

sentences.zh: 數之為用也，聖人以之觀天道焉。

translations.literal: As for the use of number, the sage employs it to observe the Way of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Number is what the sage uses to read the Way of Heaven.

translations.literal: Year, month, day, and hour are thereby completed;
translations.idiomatic: Year, month, day, and hour take their form through it;

translations.literal: yin and yang, cold and heat, are thereby regulated;
translations.idiomatic: yin and yang, cold and heat, are ordered by it;

translations.literal: the governance of the four directions proceeds thereby.
translations.idiomatic: and the governance of the four quarters proceeds from it.

sentences.zh: 夫為國家者，履端立極，必體其元；

translations.literal: For one who governs a state, to begin the year and establish the pole, one must embody its origin;
translations.idiomatic: Whoever rules a state, in inaugurating the year and fixing the cosmic pole, must take its origin as foundation;

translations.literal: in promulgating policy and examining achievement, one must follow its year;
translations.idiomatic: in promulgating policy and reviewing achievement, must follow its annual cycle;

translations.literal: in rites and music, one must rectify its new moon;
translations.idiomatic: in rites and music, must align the new moon;

translations.literal: the three farmers and the hundred crafts must be given its seasons;
translations.idiomatic: farmers and artisans must be given their proper seasons;

translations.literal: the five punishments and nine punitive expeditions must accord with its qi;
translations.idiomatic: punishments and punitive campaigns must follow its cosmic breath;

translations.literal: the myriad affairs that are undertaken must follow its sun and moon.
translations.idiomatic: and every undertaking of state must keep to its sun and moon.

sentences.zh: 六籍宗之為大典，百王執之為要道。

translations.literal: The Six Classics honor it as the great canon; the hundred kings hold it as the essential Way.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Classics enshrine it as the supreme canon; the hundred kings have held it as the essential art of rule.

sentences.zh: 是以聖人受命，必治曆數。

translations.literal: Therefore when the sage receives the Mandate, he must regulate the calendar and numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Hence when the sage receives the Mandate, he must set the calendar in order.

sentences.zh: 故得五紀有常度，庶征有常應，正朔行之於天下也。

translations.literal: Thus the Five Regulators have constant measures, the various signs have constant responses, and the new-year reckoning is carried throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Only then do the Five Regulators keep their proper measures, the portents answer as they should, and the calendar reign throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 自唐而下，凡曆數朝，亂日失天，垂將百載，天之曆數，汩陳而已矣。

translations.literal: From Tang downward, through several dynasties of calendars, days were disordered and Heaven was lost; for nearly a hundred years the celestial calendar was merely muddled and stale.
translations.idiomatic: From Tang onward, dynasty after dynasty let the calendar fall into chaos; for nearly a century Heaven's reckoning was nothing but confusion and decay.

sentences.zh: 今陛下順考古道，寅畏上天，咨詢庶官，振舉墜典。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty follows and examines the ancient Way, stands in reverent awe of Heaven above, consults the various officials, and revives fallen statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty follows the ancient Way, stands in reverent awe of Heaven, consults his ministers, and revives fallen institutions.

sentences.zh: 以臣薄遊曲藝，嘗涉舊史，遂降述作之命，俾究迎推之要，雖非能者，敢不奉詔。

translations.literal: Because your subject has lightly wandered in minor arts and once traversed old histories, you thereupon bestowed the command to compose and investigate, ordering me to plumb the essentials of welcoming and pushing forward—though no adept, how dare I not receive the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Finding in me only a modest acquaintance with these minor arts and some reading in the old histories, Your Majesty has charged me to compose a calendar and master the essentials of astronomical calculation—no master of the craft, yet how could I refuse the edict.

sentences.zh: 乃包萬象以立法，齊七政以立元，測圭箭以候氣，審朓朒以定朔，明九道以步月，校遲疾以推星，考黃道之斜正，辨天勢之升降，而交蝕詳焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon embracing the myriad images to establish law, aligning the Seven Regulators to fix the origin, measuring the gnomon and clepsydra to await the qi, examining waxing and waning to fix the new moon, clarifying the Nine Paths to pace the moon, checking slow and fast to push the stars, examining the oblique and straight of the Yellow Path, distinguishing the rising and falling of Heaven's disposition—and eclipses are thereby detailed.
translations.idiomatic: I have embraced the myriad phenomena to frame the law, aligned the seven luminaries to fix the origin, measured gnomon and clepsydra to track the seasons, refined waxing and waning to set the new moon, clarified the nine paths to pace the moon, calibrated planetary motion to reckon the stars, examined the obliquity of the ecliptic and the incline of the celestial sphere—and so made eclipses calculable in full detail.

sentences.zh: 夫立天之道，曰陰與陽，陰陽各有數，合則化成矣。

translations.literal: The Way established for Heaven is called yin and yang; yin and yang each have their number, and when combined they transform and complete.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of Heaven is yin and yang; each has its number, and when they combine, transformation is complete.

sentences.zh: 陽之策三十六，陰之策二十四，奇偶相命，兩陽三陰，同得七十二，同則陰陽之數合。

translations.literal: The yang tally is thirty-six, the yin tally twenty-four; odd and even are paired by mandate—two yang and three yin—both obtaining seventy-two; when the same, the numbers of yin and yang combine.
translations.idiomatic: The yang tally is thirty-six and the yin twenty-four; odd and even are paired by mandate—two parts yang to three yin—both yielding seventy-two, and in that sameness the yin-yang numbers unite.

sentences.zh: 七十二者，化成之數也，化成則謂之五之之數。

translations.literal: Seventy-two is the number of transformation and completion; when transformed and completed, it is called the number of the fivefold.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two is the number of completed transformation—the number of the Five Phases made whole.

sentences.zh: 五之得期之數，過者謂之氣盈，不及謂之朔虛。

translations.literal: When the fivefold obtains the number of the period, what exceeds is called surplus of qi; what falls short is called void of new moon.
translations.idiomatic: When the fivefold count reaches the period number, excess is called surplus of qi and shortfall is called void of new moon.

sentences.zh: 至於應變分用，無所不通，所謂包萬象矣。

translations.literal: As for responding to change and dividing for use, nothing is not penetrated—this is what is called embracing the myriad images.
translations.idiomatic: Applied to change and divided for use, nothing lies outside its reach—this is what it means to embrace the myriad phenomena.

sentences.zh: 故以七十二為經法，經者常也，常用之法也。

translations.literal: Therefore seventy-two is taken as the canonical method; canonical means constant—the method in constant use.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-two serves as the canonical constant—the standard method in everyday use.

sentences.zh: 法者數之節也，隨法進退，不失舊位，故謂之通法。

translations.literal: Method is the node of number; following the method in advance and retreat, one does not lose the old position—hence it is called the universal method.
translations.idiomatic: A method is a step of number; advancing and retreating by the method without losing place is called the universal method.

sentences.zh: 以通法進經法，得七千二百，謂之統法。

translations.literal: Advancing the canonical method by the universal method, one obtains seven thousand two hundred—called the systematic method.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing the canonical by the universal method yields seven thousand two hundred—the systematic method.

sentences.zh: 自元入經，先用此法，統曆之諸法也。

translations.literal: From the origin entering the canonical, this method is used first—the various methods of the systematic calendar.
translations.idiomatic: From origin to canonical reckoning, this method is applied first—it governs all methods of the systematic calendar.

sentences.zh: 以通法進統法，得七十二百萬，氣朔之下，收分必盡，謂之全率。

translations.literal: Advancing the systematic method by the universal method, one obtains seven million two hundred thousand; under qi and new moon, collecting parts must be exhausted—called the complete rate.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing the systematic by the universal method yields seven million two hundred thousand; under solar terms and new moons every fractional part is absorbed—this is the complete rate.

sentences.zh: 以通法進全率，得七千二百萬，謂之大率，而元紀生焉。

translations.literal: Advancing the complete rate by the universal method, one obtains seventy-two million—called the great rate, and the origin era is thereby born.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing the complete rate by the universal method yields seventy-two million—the great rate, from which the origin era is born.

sentences.zh: 元者，歲日月時皆甲子，日月五星，合在子正之宿，當盈縮先後之中，所謂七政齊矣。

translations.literal: The origin is when year, month, day, and hour are all jiazi, sun, moon, and the five stars all conjoin at the lodge of zi proper, standing at the mean of waxing and waning, advance and retreat—what is called the Seven Regulators aligned.
translations.idiomatic: The origin is the moment when year, month, day, and hour are all jiazi, when sun, moon, and the five planets conjoin at the zi lodge, at the mean of their varying speeds—this is the alignment of the seven luminaries.

sentences.zh: 古之植圭於陽城者，以其近洛故也，蓋尚慊其中，乃在洛之東偏。

translations.literal: The ancients planted the gnomon at Yangcheng because it was near Luoyang; they still thought it fell short of the center and so placed it on the eastern side of Luo.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients set the gnomon at Yangcheng because it lay near Luoyang—yet even then they judged it slightly east of true center.

sentences.zh: 開元十二年，遣使天下候影，南距林邑國，北距橫野軍，中得浚儀之嶽臺，應南北弦，居地之中。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kaiyuan, envoys were sent throughout the realm to observe shadows; south to the kingdom of Linyi, north to Hengye Army—in the center they obtained the Yuetai at Junyi, corresponding to the north-south chord and occupying the center of the land.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 12, observers were sent across the empire to measure shadows, from Linyi in the south to Hengye garrison in the north; at the center they found the Yuetai at Junyi, on the north-south meridian and at the heart of the land.

translations.literal: Our dynasty founded the state and fixed the capital at Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty founded the state with its capital at Liang.

sentences.zh: 今樹圭置箭，測嶽臺晷漏，以為中數，晷漏正，則日之所至，氣之所應得之矣。

translations.literal: Now we set up the gnomon and place the clepsydra, measuring the sundial and water clock of the Yuetai as the central numbers; when sundial and clepsydra are correct, then where the sun arrives and what the qi responds to are obtained.
translations.idiomatic: We now erect the gnomon and set the clepsydra, taking measurements at the Yuetai as our central standard; when sundial and water clock are true, the sun's position and the seasons' response can be read correctly.

translations.literal: Sun and moon both have waxing and waning.
translations.idiomatic: Both sun and moon vary in speed.

translations.literal: When the sun waxes and the moon wanes, the median comes late and the new moon likewise;
translations.idiomatic: When the sun is fast and the moon slow, the median hour comes late and so does the new moon;

translations.literal: when the moon waxes and the sun wanes, the median comes early and the new moon likewise.
translations.idiomatic: when the moon is fast and the sun slow, both median and new moon come early.

sentences.zh: 自古朓肭之法，率皆平行之數，入曆既有前次，而又衰稍不倫。

translations.literal: From antiquity methods for waxing and waning have all used uniform-motion numbers; entering the calendar already has prior steps, yet the decrease and increase are not proportional.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, methods for lunar speed have relied on uniform motion; though the calendar marks prior steps, the rates of change do not scale consistently.

sentences.zh: 《皇極》舊述，則迂回而難用，降及諸曆，則疏遠而多失。

translations.literal: The old account of the Huangji Calendar is circuitous and hard to use; descending to the various calendars, they are remote and full of errors.
translations.idiomatic: The old Huangji account is circuitous and impractical; later calendars are crude and error-prone.

sentences.zh: 今以月離朓朒，隨曆較定，日躔朓朒，臨用加減，所得者入離定日也。

translations.literal: Now, taking the moon's departure in waxing and waning, we compare and fix it with the calendar; for the sun's march in waxing and waning, we add and subtract as needed when applied—what is obtained is the day fixed by entering departure.
translations.idiomatic: We now fix lunar speed by comparing waxing and waning against the calendar, and adjust solar speed at the moment of use—yielding the true day of lunar departure.

sentences.zh: 一日之中，分為九限，逐限損益，衰稍有倫。

translations.literal: Within one day it is divided into nine limits; limit by limit one decreases and increases, and the waxing and waning are proportional.
translations.idiomatic: Each day is divided into nine intervals, with incremental adjustments at each step so that the rates of change follow a proper scale.

translations.literal: The method for waxing and waning is what is called exact.
translations.idiomatic: The method of waxing and waning is, in a word, exact.

sentences.zh: 赤道者，天之纮帶也，其勢圓而平，紀宿度之常數焉。

translations.literal: The Red Path is Heaven's girdle; its disposition is round and level, recording the constant numbers of lodge degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The equator is Heaven's girdle—round and level—and records the constant degrees of the lodges.

sentences.zh: 黃道者，日軌也，其半在赤道內，半在赤道外，去赤道極遠二十四度。

translations.literal: The Yellow Path is the sun's track; half lies within the Red Path, half outside, at the farthest from the Red Path by twenty-four degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The ecliptic is the sun's path: half within the equator, half without, reaching twenty-four degrees from it at maximum.

translations.literal: When it meets the Red Path, its disposition is oblique;
translations.idiomatic: Where it crosses the equator, its course is oblique;

translations.literal: when far from the Red Path, its disposition is straight.
translations.idiomatic: where it stands farthest from the equator, its course is most direct.

sentences.zh: 當斜則日行宜遲，當直則日行宜速。

translations.literal: When oblique the sun's daily motion should be slow; when straight it should be fast.
translations.idiomatic: At the oblique points the sun should move slowly; at the direct points, quickly.

sentences.zh: 故二分前後加其度，二至前後減其度。

translations.literal: Therefore before and after the two equinoxes one adds to its degrees; before and after the two solstices one subtracts.
translations.idiomatic: Hence degrees are added around the equinoxes and subtracted around the solstices.

sentences.zh: 九道者，月軌也，其半在黃道內，半在黃道外，去黃道極遠六度。

translations.literal: The Nine Paths are the moon's track; half lie within the Yellow Path, half outside, at the farthest from the Yellow Path by six degrees.
translations.idiomatic: The nine paths are the moon's track: half within the ecliptic, half without, deviating up to six degrees at maximum.

sentences.zh: 出黃道謂之正交，入黃道謂之中交。

translations.literal: Emerging from the Yellow Path is called the primary crossing; entering the Yellow Path is called the median crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Emerging from the ecliptic is the ascending node; entering it is the descending node.

sentences.zh: 若正交在秋分之宿，中交在春分之宿，則比黃道益斜。

translations.literal: If the primary crossing is at the lodge of the autumn equinox and the median crossing at the lodge of the spring equinox, then compared with the Yellow Path it is more oblique.
translations.idiomatic: If the ascending node falls at the autumn-equinox lodge and the descending at the spring-equinox lodge, the moon's path is more oblique than the sun's.

sentences.zh: 若正交在春分之宿，中交在秋分之宿，則比黃道反直。

translations.literal: If the primary crossing is at the lodge of the spring equinox and the median crossing at the lodge of the autumn equinox, then compared with the Yellow Path it is conversely straight.
translations.idiomatic: If the ascending node is at the spring-equinox lodge and the descending at the autumn-equinox lodge, the moon's path is conversely more direct than the sun's.

sentences.zh: 若正交、中交在二至之宿，則其勢差斜。

translations.literal: If primary and median crossings are at the lodges of the two solstices, then its disposition differs in obliquity.
translations.idiomatic: If both nodes fall at the solstice lodges, the obliquity differs again.

sentences.zh: 故較去二至、二分遠近，以考斜正，乃得加減之數。

translations.literal: Therefore one compares distance from the two solstices and two equinoxes to examine oblique and straight, and thereby obtains the numbers for addition and subtraction.
translations.idiomatic: By comparing distance from the solstices and equinoxes, one determines obliquity and derives the correction figures.

sentences.zh: 自古雖有九道之說，蓋亦知而未詳，空有祖述之文，全無推步之用。

translations.literal: Although from antiquity there has been talk of the Nine Paths, it was knowing yet not detailed, empty ancestral text with no use in pushing and pacing.
translations.idiomatic: The nine paths have been discussed since antiquity, but only in outline—handed-down words without real computational use.

sentences.zh: 今以黃道一周，分為八節，一節之中，分用九道，盡七十二道而復，使日月之軌，無所隱其斜正之勢焉。

translations.literal: Now, taking one circuit of the Yellow Path, dividing it into eight nodes, within one node dividing for use into nine paths, exhausting seventy-two paths and returning, so that the tracks of sun and moon nowhere hide their disposition of oblique and straight.
translations.idiomatic: We now divide the ecliptic into eight sections, each section into nine paths—seventy-two in all, cycling back—so that the tracks of sun and moon nowhere conceal their varying obliquity.

translations.literal: The method of the Nine Paths is what is called clear.
translations.idiomatic: The method of the nine paths is, in a word, clear.

sentences.zh: 星之行也，近日而疾，遠日而遲，去日極遠，勢盡而留。

translations.literal: In the motion of a star, near the sun it is fast, far from the sun slow; at the farthest from the sun its momentum is spent and it stations.
translations.idiomatic: A planet moves fastest near the sun, slowest far from it; at greatest distance its momentum is spent and it stations.

sentences.zh: 自古諸曆，分段失實，隆降無準，今日行分尚多，次日便留，自留而退，唯用平行，仍以入段行度為入曆之數，皆非本理，遂至乖戾。

translations.literal: From antiquity the various calendars, in dividing segments, lost the real; rise and fall had no standard—today's daily motion parts were still many, the next day it would station; from stationing to retrograde, only uniform motion was used, still taking the segment's motion degrees as the number for entering the calendar—none accorded with the root principle, and thus reached perversity.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier calendars misjudged the segments, with no proper scale for acceleration and deceleration—a planet still moving quickly one day would station the next, and from station to retrograde only uniform motion was assumed, using segment degrees as calendar entries. None of this matched nature, and error piled on error.

sentences.zh: 今校定逐日行分，積逐日行分以為變段。

translations.literal: Now we compare and fix the daily motion parts day by day, accumulating daily motion parts to form variable segments.
translations.idiomatic: We now fix the daily motion part by part, accumulating them into variable segments.

sentences.zh: 於是自疾漸而遲，勢盡而留，自留而行，亦積微而後多。

translations.literal: Thereby from fast it gradually becomes slow, momentum spent it stations; from stationing to direct motion, it also accumulates minutely before becoming much.
translations.idiomatic: Thus speed gradually gives way to slowness, momentum is spent and the planet stations; from station to direct motion, minute increments build until motion is swift again.

sentences.zh: 別立諸段變曆，以推變差，俾諸段變差際會相合，星之遲疾，可得而知之矣。

translations.literal: Separately establishing variable calendars for the various segments to push the variable discrepancy, so that the variable discrepancies of the various segments meet and accord, the star's slow and fast may thereby be known.
translations.idiomatic: Separate variable tables are set up for each segment to calculate the discrepancies, so that segment by segment the figures align—and the planet's varying speed can be known with precision.

sentences.zh: 自古相傳，皆謂去交十五度以下，則日月有蝕，殊不知日月之相掩，與暗虛之所射，其理有異焉。

translations.literal: Handed down from antiquity, all say that within fifteen degrees of departure from crossing, sun and moon will have an eclipse—yet they did not know that the mutual masking of sun and moon and the casting of the dark void have principles that differ.
translations.idiomatic: Tradition held that within fifteen degrees of nodal departure, sun and moon would eclipse—yet they did not grasp that mutual occultation of sun and moon and casting of the dark void follow different principles.

sentences.zh: 今以日月徑度之大小，校去交之遠近，以黃道之斜正，天勢之升降，度仰視旁視之分數，則交虧得其實矣。

translations.literal: Now by comparing the great and small of sun and moon diameters, calibrating nearness and distance from crossing, the oblique and straight of the Yellow Path, the rise and fall of Heaven's disposition, and the fractional degrees of overhead and side viewing, the loss at crossing is thereby obtained in reality.
translations.idiomatic: By comparing sun and moon diameters, calibrating nodal distance, ecliptic obliquity, celestial disposition, and overhead versus side-view fractions, eclipse magnitude is obtained in reality.
